sections.title: What this material connects
sections.text: Artin’s course links abstract algebra and geometry. The reviewed handout asks which discrete plane-symmetry groups can have a two-dimensional translation lattice and point group containing only identity and one reflection.

sections.title: Main result of the handout
sections.text: There are three group types under this classification. The permitted lattice has a rectangular form or a centered variant; translation and reflection data determine which types remain distinct.

sections.title: Proof architecture
sections.text: Reflection sends lattice vectors to lattice vectors. Adding and subtracting reflected vectors produces horizontal and vertical constraints. Then a nontranslation motion is written as a translation followed by reflection; squaring it constrains its glide component.

sections.title: Why the last step matters
sections.text: Two lattice possibilities and two motion possibilities initially suggest four cases. A coordinate adjustment identifies the centered-lattice glide case with a reflection case, leaving three types.

sections.title: How to connect it to shape experiments
sections.text: Distinguish a finite point group from the whole periodic symmetry group. The translation lattice carries information that a list of rotations and reflections alone cannot express.
